title: IIT Bombay Suicide: Abetment Case Against Professor After Father Alleges Casteist Slurs
excerpt: Sahil Wakode was found dead hours after being caught using ChatGPT in an exam; his father now alleges months of caste-based harassment by Professor Suryanarayan Dulla, and the case has moved to the Mumbai Crime Branch.
body:
• In a sharp escalation of the case, the father of Sahil Wakode — the IIT Bombay student found dead in his hostel room on September 18, hours after being caught using ChatGPT in an exam — has filed a formal police complaint alleging months of caste-based harassment.
  • Mumbai Police have registered an abetment-of-suicide case against Professor Suryanarayan Dulla, the exam invigilator, along with provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act; two other accused are unidentified in the FIR.
  • The investigation has been transferred to the Mumbai Crime Branch, to be led by an ACP-rank officer; IIT Bombay says it will cooperate fully and maintains no disciplinary action was initiated against the student.

The death of an IIT Bombay student on September 18 has taken a grave new turn. The father of Sahil Wakode, a second-year student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering from Yavatmal, Maharashtra, has filed a formal police complaint alleging that his son faced severe mental harassment and casteist slurs over the past three months — allegations that have led to an abetment-of-suicide case against a professor and the transfer of the probe to the Mumbai Crime Branch.

Wakode was found dead in his Powai campus hostel room on Friday evening, hours after being caught using a mobile phone during an exam — he had allegedly uploaded the question paper to ChatGPT to seek answers. IIT Bombay has said the exam instructor and the Head of Department counselled him and assured him the incident would not affect his academic career, with no disciplinary action initiated. Mumbai Police initially filed an Accident Death Report; on September 19, as student protests erupted on campus, an FIR was registered against persons linked to the exam incident.

"Wakode's mother said: "My son has been killed."

The father's complaint

On September 20, the case escalated. Wakode's father, Ravindra Chakradhar Wankhade, alleged in his complaint that Professor Suryanarayan Dulla — who was also the invigilator during the exam — hurled caste-based abuses at his son and, on one occasion, allegedly threatened him, saying that because he belonged to a "lower caste," he could easily implicate him in a false case. The father further alleged the harassment had continued for three months, at the direction of Director Shireesh B Kedare. Wakode's mother said: "My son has been killed. He was severely harassed. I want justice."

Police have registered the case under Section 108 (abetment of suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, along with provisions of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, covering intentional insult or intimidation of a member of an SC/ST community. Two other accused remain unidentified in the FIR. All of the caste-abuse allegations come from the father's complaint; they are claims, not findings, and the investigation is underway.

The institute's position — and the protests

IIT Bombay has expressed grief and said it will cooperate fully with the authorities. Its official statement maintains the sequence it described on September 19: "No disciplinary action was initiated against the student. The matter was also discussed with the student by the instructor and the Head of the Department, who counselled him and assured him that the incident would not adversely affect his academic career." The institute has disputed key allegations by the family and students, according to education reporting.

Students have been protesting on campus, with demands including action against the professor and calls for the director to quit. Police found no suicide note, and the post-mortem was pending at last report.

A wider pattern

This is the third student suicide on the IIT Bombay campus in roughly seven months — a second-year student died in his hostel room in February, and a 20-year-old second-year BTech student in July. Caste discrimination and student suicides at elite Indian institutions are a recurring national controversy, and the invocation of the SC/ST Act against an IIT professor in this case has intensified scrutiny of academic pressure, disciplinary practices and student mental-health support on campus.

What's next

The Crime Branch investigation, led by an ACP-rank officer, will now determine whether the evidence supports the charges — including the allegation of sustained caste-based harassment, which the institute disputes. With the campus protests continuing and a third death in seven months, the pressure on IIT Bombay to demonstrate concrete changes to its student-welfare systems is unlikely to ease regardless of how the criminal case unfolds.
